## RINO hunting

![Reposted to Truth Social by Donald Trump, May 2026.](figures/trump_rino_truthsocial.jpg)

## Puzzle

::: incremental
- Shift in intraparty power

  - From durable institution to personalist rule

    - Strongman leader

- Trump's RINO attacks

  - On Republicans' *partisan legitimacy*

    - Reframes disloyalty to Trump as disloyalty to an institution

      - Novel form of *presidential party discipline*

        - Successful where past presidents failed

        - Transforming party identity
:::

## Outline

- Situate our contribution

- Theory of presidential party discipline

- Hypotheses

- Research design

- Findings

- Takeaways and implications

## Our contribution

![](figures/rino_lit.drawio.png){fig-align="center"}

## Presidential party discipline

![](figures/party_concept_map.drawio.png){fig-align="center" width="8in"}

## Presidential party discipline

::: incremental
- Presidential dilemma when "going public" against co-partisans

  - Short-sighted, divisive, petty

    <br>

- Strategically advantageous to frame intraparty opponents as *traitors*

  - Turning against a collective organization and shared identity
:::

## Hypotheses

Presidential attacks on co-partisans will be associated with:

::: incremental
1.  A decline in the targeted officeholder’s campaign fundraising.

    <br>

2.  The entry of substantial primary challengers in the next election cycle.

    <br>

3.  Officeholder exit due to either losing renomination or retiring.

    <br>

4.  Primary challenges and exit from office as the number of attacks increases.
:::

## Research design

::: incremental
- Collected every instance of Trump's use of RINO (N = 318) since 2015

  - Social media

  - Speeches

  - Press

- Hand-coded for targets

  - Individual

  - Group

  - Vague

- Descriptive and associational analysis
:::

# Findings

## *Who is a RINO?*

```{r}
events_with_people <- all_events |>
  inner_join(rino_events |> select(event_id, person_id = rino_attack), by = "event_id") |>
  inner_join(people_name_id, by = "person_id")

events_with_people |>
  count(name, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  mutate(
    officeholder = if_else(
      name %in% filter(events_with_people, person_id %in% rino_officeholders$person_id)$name,
      "Yes", "No")
  ) |>
  rename(Name = name, Attacks = n, Officeholder = officeholder) |> 
  ggplot(aes(y = fct_reorder(Name, Attacks), x = Attacks, 
             fill = factor(Officeholder))) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(y = "", 
       title = "Top 10 RINO targets", 
       fill = "Officeholder") +
  theme(plot.title.position = "plot", 
        legend.position = "bottom") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2", direction = -1)
```

## *Who is a RINO?*

```{r}
meta_all <- read_csv("~/Desktop/Desktop/Conferences/APSA 2026/rino_officeholder_metadata.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

officeholder_events <- events_with_people |>
  filter(person_id %in% rino_officeholders$person_id)

attack_counts_all <- officeholder_events |>
  count(person_id, name = "n_attacks")

oh_all <- meta_all |>
  left_join(
    rino_officeholders |> rename(officeholder = officeholder_rino_name),
    by = "officeholder"
  ) |>
  left_join(attack_counts_all, by = "person_id") |>
  mutate(
    n_attacks = replace_na(n_attacks, 0),
    level = case_when(
      chamber %in% c("House", "Senate")                          ~ "Federal",
      chamber %in% c("State House", "State Senate",
                     "Statewide", "Local", "Presidential")       ~ "State",
      TRUE                                                        ~ NA_character_
    ),
    office_type = case_when(
      chamber == "House"                             ~ "U.S. House",
      chamber == "Senate"                            ~ "U.S. Senate",
      chamber %in% c("Statewide", "Presidential")   ~ office,
      chamber == "State House"                       ~ "State House",
      chamber == "State Senate"                      ~ "State Senate",
      TRUE                                           ~ chamber
    )
  )

library(PrettyCols)
oh_all |>
  count(level, office_type) |>
  arrange(level, desc(n)) |>
  rename(Level = level, `Office type` = office_type, N = n) |> 
  filter_out(`Office type` == "Candidate") |> 
  ggplot(aes(y = reorder(`Office type`, N), x = N, fill = `Office type`)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
    
```

# *Electoral consequences of RINO attacks*

## Campaign finance -- large donors

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)

rdit  <- read_csv("~/Desktop/Desktop/Conferences/APSA 2026/rdit_dataset.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
meta  <- read_csv("~/Desktop/Desktop/Conferences/APSA 2026/rino_officeholder_metadata.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
posts <- read_csv("~/Desktop/Desktop/Conferences/APSA 2026/rino_posts.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Treated officials only; exclude those with no federal committee (Hogan, O'Dea, Ricketts)
df <- rdit |>
  filter(is_treated == 1, !is.na(daily_total_receipts)) |>
  mutate(
    log_total  = log1p(daily_total_receipts),
    post_attack = as.integer(post_attack)
  )

# Flag officials whose committee was entirely dormant during their attack window
dormant <- df |>
  group_by(officeholder) |>
  summarise(has_receipts = any(daily_total_receipts > 0), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(!has_receipts) |>
  pull(officeholder)

# Active sample: officials with at least some fundraising activity
df_active <- df |> filter(!officeholder %in% dormant)

# Small-dollar analysis samples (WinRed conduit)
treated_active <- rdit |>
  filter(is_treated == 1, !is.na(daily_small_dollar_receipts)) |>
  group_by(officeholder) |>
  filter(any(daily_total_receipts > 0 | daily_small_dollar_receipts > 0)) |>
  ungroup()

sd_active <- treated_active |>
  group_by(officeholder) |>
  filter(any(daily_small_dollar_receipts > 0)) |>
  ungroup()

df_active |>
  group_by(days_from_attack) |>
  summarise(mean_log = mean(log_total), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = days_from_attack, y = mean_log)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, color = "#C0392B", alpha = 0.75, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = Inf,
           label = "Attack date", vjust = 1.5, hjust = 0, size = 5, color = "grey8", family = "Roboto") +
  labs(
    x = "Days from attack",
    y = "log(mean daily receipts)"
  ) +
  geom_smooth(se = F, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = log1p(c(0, 20, 40, 60, 80)),
    labels = scales::dollar(c(0, 20, 40, 60, 80))
  )
```

## Large donors — House members

```{r}
per_official <- df_active |>
  group_by(officeholder) |>
  filter(attack_date == max(attack_date)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(officeholder) |>
  summarise(
    pre_mean  = mean(daily_total_receipts[post_attack == 0], na.rm = TRUE),
    post_mean = mean(daily_total_receipts[post_attack == 1], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(meta |> select(officeholder, chamber), by = "officeholder") |>
  mutate(
    change    = post_mean - pre_mean,
    direction = if_else(change >= 0, "Increase", "Decrease"),
    label     = fct_reorder(officeholder, change)
  )

per_official |>
  filter(chamber == "House") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = change, y = label, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey30") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2", direction = -1) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = dollar) +
  labs(x = "Change in mean daily receipts", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Primaries and retirement

```{r}
cycle_panel <- read_csv("~/Desktop/Desktop/Conferences/APSA 2026/cycle_panel_with_outcomes.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

state_outcomes_raw <- read_csv("~/Desktop/Desktop/Conferences/APSA 2026/state_officeholder_outcomes.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

official_level <- cycle_panel |>
  filter(is_treated == 1, !is.na(bioname)) |>
  group_by(bioname) |>
  summarise(
    any_substantial = any(substantial_challenge == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    worst_outcome   = case_when(
      any(outcome == "lost_primary", na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Lost primary",
      any(outcome == "retired",      na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Retired",
      any(outcome == "won_primary",  na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Won primary",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(worst_outcome))

state_for_combined <- state_outcomes_raw |>
  mutate(
    level     = "State/Local",
    challenge = factor(
      if_else(any_substantial, "Substantial\n(\u2265 25%)", "Not\nsubstantial\n(< 25%)"),
      levels = c("Substantial\n(\u2265 25%)", "Not\nsubstantial\n(< 25%)")
    ),
    outcome_f = factor(
      case_when(
        worst_outcome == "Won primary"  ~ "Won\nprimary",
        worst_outcome == "Lost primary" ~ "Lost\nprimary",
        TRUE                            ~ "Retired"
      ),
      levels = c("Won\nprimary", "Retired", "Lost\nprimary")
    )
  )

fed_for_combined <- official_level |>
  mutate(
    level     = "Federal",
    challenge = factor(
      if_else(any_substantial, "Substantial\n(\u2265 25%)", "Not\nsubstantial\n(< 25%)"),
      levels = c("Substantial\n(\u2265 25%)", "Not\nsubstantial\n(< 25%)")
    ),
    outcome_f = factor(
      case_when(
        worst_outcome == "Won primary"  ~ "Won\nprimary",
        worst_outcome == "Lost primary" ~ "Lost\nprimary",
        TRUE                            ~ "Retired"
      ),
      levels = c("Won\nprimary", "Retired", "Lost\nprimary")
    )
  )

combined_long <- bind_rows(
  fed_for_combined   |> select(level, challenge, outcome_f),
  state_for_combined |> select(level, challenge, outcome_f)
) |>
  mutate(level = factor(level, levels = c("Federal", "State/Local")))

combined_alluvial <- combined_long |>
  count(level, challenge, outcome_f, name = "freq") |> mutate(
    level = fct_recode(level, "State" = "State/Local")
  )


ggplot(combined_alluvial,
       aes(axis1 = level, axis2 = challenge, axis3 = outcome_f, y = freq)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = outcome_f), alpha = 0.72, width = 1/4) +
  geom_stratum(width = 1/4, fill = "white", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(
    stat = "stratum",
    aes(label = paste0(after_stat(stratum), "\n(n = ", after_stat(count), ")")),
    size = 4, lineheight = 1.1, family = "Roboto"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Won\nprimary" = "#4dab6d", "Retired" = "#f4a942",
               "Lost\nprimary" = "#c0392b"),
    guide  = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = c("level", "challenge", "outcome_f"),
    labels = c("Level", "Primary challenge", "Outcome"),
    expand = c(0.15, 0.15)
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 22, base_family = "Roboto") +
  theme(
    text         = element_text(color = "#131516"),
    axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid   = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x  = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, family = "Roboto", color = "#131516"),
    plot.margin  = margin(5, 10, 5, 10)
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

## Attack intensity

```{r}
cycle_panel |>
  filter(is_treated == 1, is_election_year == TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    cumulative_attacks_corrected = replace_na(cumulative_attacks_corrected, 0),
    outcome_label = case_when(
      outcome == "won_primary"  ~ "Won primary",
      outcome == "lost_primary" ~ "Lost primary",
      outcome == "retired"      ~ "Retired",
      TRUE                      ~ "Won primary"
    ),
    attack_tier = cut(cumulative_attacks_corrected,
                      breaks = c(-Inf, 0, 2, Inf),
                      labels = c("1", "2–3", "3+"))
  ) |>
  count(attack_tier, outcome_label) |>
  mutate(outcome_label = factor(outcome_label,
                                levels = c("Won primary", "Retired", "Lost primary"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = attack_tier, y = n, fill = outcome_label)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Won primary" = "#4dab6d", "Retired" = "#f4a942",
               "Lost primary" = "#c0392b")
  ) +
  labs(x = "Pre-primary RINO attacks",
       y = "Number of observations",
       fill = "Outcome") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Takeaways and implications

## Takeaways

::: incremental
- Trump’s RINO rhetoric has swelled over time.

  <br>

- Directed at a heterogeneous set of targets.

  <br>

- Electoral consequences of being targeted are also mixed.
:::

## Implications

::: incremental
- How durable a shift in party power?

  - Trump’s RINO rhetoric may be as unique as he is.

    <br>

- Party asymmetry

  - No comparable DINO phenomenon.

    <br>

- The true effect of interest

  - To what extent does Trump’s RINO hunting affect *all* Republicans?
:::
